sourceType: Official Rajasthan Tourism website (Government of Rajasthan)
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Chittorgarh Fort stands atop a 180m hill, spread across 700 acres. Faced three major sieges: 1303 by Ala-ud-din Khilji (Sultan of Delhi), 1533 by Bahadur Shah (Sultan of Gujarat), and 1568 by Mughal Emperor Akbar; returned to the Rajputs in 1616 under Mughal Emperor Jahangir.

places.name: Light & Sound Show at Chittorgarh Fort
places.facts: DMX-controlled LED luminaries, gobo lights, 5.1 surround sound; depicts the fort's history, rulers, wars, and Alauddin Khilji's attack; runs after sunset. Contact 01472 241238.

places.name: Vijay Stambh (Tower of Victory)
places.facts: Built by Maharana Kumbha 1440-1448 AD to commemorate his victory over the Muslim rulers of Malwa and Gujarat; nine-storey tower, part red sandstone and part white marble, covered in sculptures of Hindu gods and goddesses; narrow internal stairs lead to a terrace with panoramic town views.

places.name: Kirti Stambh (Tower of Fame)
places.facts: Dedicated to Adinathji, the first Jain Tirthankara; adorned with Digambar monk figures; seven-storey tower built by a wealthy Jain merchant in the 12th century AD; near the Jain temples of Nemi Nath ji, Adinath ji, and Parshwanath ji.

places.name: Fateh Prakash Palace (Government Museum)
places.facts: Built by Maharana Fateh Singh as his residence, Rajput-style architecture; now a museum with wood crafts from Bassi village, post-medieval Jain Ambica/Indra statues from Rashmi village, weapons, clay tribal-costume replicas, paintings, and crystal ware. Timings 9:45am-4:45pm; entry Rs.20 (Indian), Rs.10 (child), Rs.100 (foreigner), Rs.50 (foreigner child).

places.name: Jain Temples (Chittorgarh Fort)
places.facts: Six Jain temples within the fort walls; the largest is the Bhagawan Adinatha temple with 52 devkulikas; Satbees Deori Jain Temple (named for 27 deities) sits opposite Badi Pol.

places.name: Kalika Mata Temple
places.facts: Built 8th century AD, originally a sun-god temple; rebuilt by Rana Hameer in the 14th century and rededicated to Goddess Kali.

places.name: Tulja Bhawani Temple
places.facts: Dedicated to Goddess Durga; built by Banveer in the 16th century; legend ties its name to a Tula Dan (weight-equal donation) by Banveer; later associated with the Maratha goddess Tulja Bhavani during their period of dominance over the fort.

places.name: Gaumukh Reservoir
places.facts: Deep spring-fed tank; the spring emerges from a rock formation resembling a Gaumukh ('cow's mouth'); considered sacred locally.

places.name: Ratan Singh Palace
places.facts: Winter palace of the royal family, overlooking a small lake; fairly rundown but popular with visitors.

places.name: Rana Kumbha Palace
places.facts: One of the fort's most massive ruined monuments; restored by Maharana Kumbha (hence 'Kumbha Mahal') though the original predates him; main entrance is the currently-closed Tripolia Darwaza; includes Suraj Gokhada, Janana Mahal, Kanwarpada's palaces, and underground dungeons linked to Jauhar accounts.

places.name: Kumbha Shyam Temple
places.facts: Built 8th century, originally dedicated to Varaha (boar avatar); renovated by Maharana Kumbha in the 15th century, who installed the Kumbhashyam idol; Indo-Aryan architectural style.

places.name: Meerabai Temple
places.facts: Site where Meerabai, devotee of Krishna, worshipped; classic North Indian temple style, raised plinth, conical roof visible from afar, four small corner pavilions around an open porch.

places.name: Menal Temple & Waterfall
places.location: 80 km from Bhilwara, on Bhilwara-Kota road
places.facts: Waterfall dropping 150m into a V-shaped valley; best visited July-October.

places.name: Nagari
places.location: 18 km north of Chittorgarh, on the Berach river
places.facts: Ancient town known as Majhimika/Madhyamika, named in a Barli inscription dated 443 BC; flourished Mauryan through Gupta periods; ruled successively by Sibi tribes, Western Kshatrapas, Malavas, and Huna king; excavated punch-marked coins; attractions include an ancient Shiva Temple, Hathiyon ka Bara, and Ubhdivat (Prakash Stambh).

places.name: Bhainsrorgarh Fort
places.location: 235 km NE of Udaipur, 50 km south of Kota
places.facts: Perched on a 200 ft slate ridge surrounded by the Chambal and Brahmani rivers; built by Rawat Lal Singh II, granted as jagir by Maharana Jagat Singh II of Mewar in 1741 AD; believed to originate 2nd century AD; possibly attacked by Allauddin Khilji; now a heritage hotel.

places.name: Baroli Temples
places.location: Rawatbhata, 115 km from Chittorgarh, confluence of Brahmani and Chambal rivers
places.facts: Built by Huna rulers in the 9th century; main temple is Ghatseshwar Mahadev, plus 9 other temples in the complex; Shringar Chauri marks the marriage site of Mewar ruler Allaat and Huna princess Hariyadevi, connecting the Guhila and Huna dynasties.

places.name: Jaimal and Patta's Palace/Cenotaph
places.facts: Commemorates Rathod Jaimal and Sisodia Patta, who defended the fort in Akbar's 1567 siege while Maharana Uday Singh's family fled to the hills; both died in the defense; Akbar ordered statues of them on elephants outside Agra Fort (later removed by Aurangzeb); a cenotaph marks the spot in Chittorgarh.

places.name: Bhamashah Ki Haveli
places.location: In front of the Topkhana, Chittorgarh
places.facts: Home of Bhamashah, key minister and financier to Maharana Pratap; he and brother Tarachand funded Pratap's Mughal resistance after he ran out of funds, including around the Battle of Haldighati; ASI-maintained; pillared entrance verandah, rooms up to three floors; near a Mahadev temple, Moti Bazaar, and Nagina Bazaar; low footfall.

places.name: Sanwaliya Ji Temple
places.location: Mandafiya village, on the Chittorgarh-Udaipur Highway
places.facts: Major pilgrimage site; origin tied to a shepherd's 1840 dream leading to the excavation of three idols near Bhadsauda-Bagund village; the grandest of the three temples, Sanwaliya ji Dham, is at Mandafiya. Darshan timings: Mangla Arati 5:30am, Rajbhog 10-11:15am, Arati 2:30pm, Arati 8-9:15pm, Bhajan 9:15-11pm.

places.name: Bassi Village
places.facts: 16th-century medieval fort ruins, Shiva Sagar Kund and temples; known for wooden-art 'Kavad' temples depicting mythological stories.

places.name: Samidheshwar Temple
places.facts: Built 11th century by Parmar Raja Bhoj of Malwa; also called Tribhavannarayan/Bhoj Jagti; visited by Solanki king Kumarpal of Gujarat after defeating Arneraj Chauhan of Ajmer in 1150 AD; renovated by Maharana Mokal in 1428 (hence 'Mokal ji's temple'); its three-faced Shiva idol resembles the main idol at Elephanta Caves, Mumbai.

places.name: Bassi Wildlife Sanctuary
places.facts: Established 1988, in the Vindhyan hill range; former royal hunting ground with old Audhis (hunting towers); Chital, Sambar, common fox, wild boar, leopard; Orai, Bassi, Sarana sites notable for migratory birds including Sarus Crane.

places.name: Sita Mata Wildlife Sanctuary
places.facts: Only forest with building-grade teak trees (~50% of vegetation), plus salar, tendu, amla, bamboo, bel; Jakham and Karmoj rivers flow through; leopard, hyena, jackal, fox, porcupine, spotted deer, wild bear, four-horned antelope, nilgai; notable for the flying squirrel.

howToReach.air: Maharana Pratap Airport, Dabok (Udaipur), ~90 km away
howToReach.rail: Well connected to Udaipur, Jaipur, Ajmer, Ratlam, Delhi, Kota and other major cities
howToReach.road: Regular buses from all major cities in Rajasthan
